rationale: CR 306.7 states the old noncombat-damage redirection to planeswalkers was removed, so a spell that damages a player can't hit planeswalkers; 115.4 states which objects damage spells may target.

508.1/508.1a set out that the attack declaration is a sequence of steps and that the chosen creatures must be legal choices; 508.1d states that when a creature can't attack unless a cost is paid, the player is not required to pay it.

702.37e and 116.2b state that turning a face-down permanent face up is a special action whose cost is the morph cost; 118.8 states additional costs are paid alongside a spell's mana cost or an ability's activation cost, so Exiled Doomsayer's {2} is a morph-cost increase, not an additional cost.
113.8 states the controller of an activated ability is the player who activated it, so Anabella controls Moonring Island's mana ability and False Dawn's effect applies to the mana it produces.
602.1 defines an activated ability as '[Cost]: [Effect]' and 605.1 limits which abilities are mana abilities; Channel's granted action is neither, so Phyrexian Revoker doesn't stop it.
729.2 states the subgame proceeds like a normal game following rule 103, and 729.4 states main-game objects are outside the subgame, so the main-game player-control effect doesn't carry into it.

609.4 states an 'as though' effect applies only to its stated effect and the game is otherwise treated normally, and 609.4b states spend-as-though effects change only how a cost may be paid; both effects therefore apply at once.

502.3 states the untap turn-based action in which the active player determines which permanents untap; Undiscovered Paradise's return happens as part of that action, and effects stopping the untap don't stop it.

712.9 (with its Cytoshape example) states a double-faced permanent that is a copy of something else still transforms and remains that copy, and 712.18 states effects continue to apply after transforming; 701.27e states 'transforms into [characteristic]' abilities trigger based on the object immediately after it transforms.
303.4f states that an Aura entering the battlefield other than by resolving as an Aura spell has its controller choose a legal object to enchant as it enters, with no targeting involved.

116.2c states that paying to end a continuous effect is a special action available for as long as the effect allows it; 609.1 states effects are created when the spell or ability resolves, so the option doesn't exist until the Licid ability has resolved.
208.3 states a noncreature permanent has no power, and 208.5 states an object with no value for power has power 0, so the power comparison in Old Man of the Sea's duration uses 0.

608.2h states an effect needing information about an object that has left its zone uses last known information, so the toughness it had on the battlefield is used; 120.3e states damage is merely marked on a creature and doesn't reduce toughness.
723.1 states a player-control effect applies to the next turn the affected player actually takes and lasts that entire turn; 500.7 states extra turns are added directly after the specified turn.

614.1d states that continuous effects reading '[Objects] enter the battlefield ...' are replacement effects, so Uphill Battle applies to Dryad Arbor as a creature entering; 305.9 states an object that is both a land and another card type is played as a land.

614.17a states 'can't' effects must exist before the event and can't go back in time, and 614.4 says the same for replacement effects; Solemnity's effect doesn't exist until it has entered, which is simultaneous with Phylactery Lich.

614.17a and 614.4 state such effects must already exist before the event, so Suncleanser's effect still applied immediately before Phylactery Lich entered; 614.12a states choices for enter-the-battlefield replacement effects (Hellkite Hatchling's devour sacrifice) are made before the permanent enters.

614.17a (and 614.4 for replacement effects generally) states these effects must exist before the event; Tatterkite still had its can't-have-counters ability immediately before Phylactery Lich entered, because Humility enters simultaneously.
608.2c states a spell's instructions are followed in the order written, so Leonin Arbiter is exiled and its effect ends before the search instruction happens.

603.10a states leaves-the-battlefield abilities look back in time, so Slimefoot's ability triggers even though it died too; 702.15c states last known information determines whether the source had lifelink as it deals damage.

708.2 states a face-down permanent has no characteristics beyond those granted by the face-down rules, so Blightsteel Colossus had no replacement ability; 614.4 states replacement effects must exist before the event they would replace.

702.51a states convoke lets you tap one creature rather than pay each individual mana in the spell's total cost, and 702.51b states convoke applies only after the total cost is determined, so no more creatures than the cost calls for may be tapped.
608.2n states an instant or sorcery goes to its owner's graveyard only as the final part of its resolution, so Beacon Bolt isn't in the graveyard while it counts cards there.
508.3a states 'whenever [a creature] attacks' abilities don't trigger if the creature is put onto the battlefield attacking; 508.4 states such creatures are attacking but never 'attacked.'

701.44b states a permanent 'explores' only after the whole explore process is complete; 603.10 states trigger conditions are determined from the objects and continuous effects existing immediately after the event, so the newly gained text is already present.
603.10 states objects that exist immediately after an event are checked against trigger conditions, so Blood Operative sitting in the graveyard after the surveil is checked for its surveil trigger.

608.2c states Merfolk Trickster's instructions are followed in the order written, so the tap happens before abilities are lost; 603.2 and 603.3 state the ability triggers automatically at that moment and is then put on the stack regardless of what happens afterward.

109.2b states 'spell' means an object on the stack, so Soulfire Grand Master's lifelink grant never reaches Kozilek's Return in the graveyard; 113.6 and 113.6k state a trigger condition that can't trigger from the battlefield functions in the zone it can trigger from, which is how the graveyard ability works without the card being cast.

603.3b states a player puts their simultaneously triggered abilities on the stack in any order they choose; 118.12 states a 'you may pay [cost]. If you do' cost is paid when the ability resolves, not when it goes on the stack.

603.12 states reflexive triggered abilities are created during resolution and trigger afterward, so Hypothesizzle has already left the stack; 702.15c states lifelink is determined from the source's last known information.

614.16 states that 'if an effect would create one or more tokens' replacement effects apply when a resolving spell creates a token, so Crafty Cutpurse's effect (itself now under Nylah's control) applies to Beast Attack's token; 111.2 states a token enters under the control of the player who creates it.
118.6 states an object with no mana cost has an unpayable cost and that attempting to pay one is an illegal action; 601.2h states unpayable costs can't be paid.

607.2a states the exile ability and the ability referring to 'the exiled card' are linked; 607.3 states that when the linked ability exiled multiple cards the singular reference gets multiple answers, and the sum is used to determine a variable.

614.10 states skipping a turn is a replacement effect and that a turn can no longer be skipped once it has started, so the choice is made before the turn begins; 723.1 states the control effect covers the controlled turn itself.

608.2h and 608.2i state that an effect needing information about an object uses last known information and doesn't require the object to still be in the zone it was in, so Predict only cares whether the card has the chosen name.

616.1b states a replacement effect that changes under whose control an object enters must be applied first; 616.1f (and 614.12) state the process then repeats considering only effects that are still applicable, so Essence of the Wild no longer applies to a creature entering under an opponent's control.
109.2 states a description that includes a card type or subtype without 'card' or a named zone means a permanent on the battlefield, so Pulmonic Sliver's ability covers only Sliver permanents.
500.7 states that effects giving a player extra turns add them directly after the specified turn; any turn created by a spell or ability that way is an extra turn.

701.19a states a regeneration shield replaces only the next destruction this turn; 608.2c states Austere Command's chosen modes are carried out in the order written, so the shield is spent on the artifact destruction and gone by the creature destruction.
603.2e states 'becomes' triggers fire only when the named event happens and don't retrigger if the state already exists; 115.7a states a target can only be changed to another legal target.

616.1 and 616.1e state that the affected object's controller chooses which applicable replacement effect to apply, with no forced order between these two; 616.1f states the process repeats using only effects that are still applicable, which is why Furnace of Rath may end up not applying at all.

707.2b states that once an object has been copied, later changes to the original's copiable values don't change the copy; 712.9 states only permanents represented by double-faced cards or tokens can transform.
805.6a states that when multiple players draw in a shared-team-turns game, each player on the active team performs their draws in whatever order that team likes.

115.9b states an object checking a '[spell] that targets [something]' uses the targets' current state and ignores a target no longer in its expected zone; 608.2b states an ability whose targets are all illegal doesn't resolve.
510.4 states the creatures that assign damage in the second combat damage step are those that had neither first strike nor double strike as the first combat damage step began.

614.12a states a choice required by an enter-the-battlefield replacement effect is made before the permanent enters; 101.4 and 101.4b state simultaneous choices are made in APNAP order with later players knowing the earlier choices, so both cards are known before they enter.
702.34a states flashback is an alternative cost; 118.9a and 601.2b state only one alternative cost may be applied to a spell as it's cast.

701.3b states attaching an Equipment to what it's already attached to does nothing, and 701.3c/613.7e state a new timestamp comes only from attaching to a different object; 613.7 states the later timestamp is applied last, so Tightening Coils still wins.
103.5 states the starting player declares whether they'll take a mulligan first and each other player then does so in turn order, so Albert acts before Nico has declared.
103.6 states opening-hand actions may be taken only once the mulligan process is complete.
